answer: Reputation is a scarce, unforgeable resource earned by consistently passing originality checks, and the economy spends it to filter out Sybil clusters before they can compound into a majority. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock.. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. Consider a spiral as the anchor of the cost. A thread stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a crystal hold...
